title: Ceftriaxone for Injection, USP — FDA Prescribing Information (Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc.) [DailyMed]

claims.text: Ceftriaxone is FDA-indicated for meningitis caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria meningitidis, or Streptococcus pneumoniae.
claims.byte_quote: MENINGITIS caused by Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria meningitidis or Streptococcus pneumoniae.

claims.text: Ceftriaxone has also been used successfully in a limited number of meningitis and shunt-infection cases caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis and Escherichia coli.
claims.byte_quote: Ceftriaxone for Injection, USP has also been used successfully in a limited number of cases of meningitis and shunt infection caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis 1 and Escherichia coli. 1

claims.text: Pediatric meningitis dosing: initial therapeutic dose 100 mg/kg (max 4 g), then 100 mg/kg/day (max 4 g/day), once daily or divided every 12 hours, for a usual duration of 7 to 14 days.
claims.byte_quote: In the treatment of meningitis, it is recommended that the initial therapeutic dose be 100 mg/kg (not to exceed 4 grams). Thereafter, a total daily dose of 100 mg/‌kg/‌day (not to exceed 4 grams daily) is recommended. The daily dose may be administered once a day (or in equally divided doses every 12 hours). The usual duration of therapy is 7 to 14 days.

claims.text: For serious non-meningitis pediatric infections, the recommended total daily dose is 50 to 75 mg/kg in divided doses every 12 hours, not to exceed 2 g/day — distinguishing the higher meningitis (CNS) dose from the general indication.
claims.byte_quote: For the treatment of serious miscellaneous infections other than meningitis, the recommended total daily dose is 50 to 75 mg/kg, given in divided doses every 12 hours. The total daily dose should not exceed 2 grams.

claims.text: Usual adult daily dose is 1 to 2 g once daily (or divided twice daily) depending on infection type and severity, not to exceed 4 g/day (general adult indication, not meningitis-specific).
claims.byte_quote: The usual adult daily dose is 1 to 2 grams given once a day (or in equally divided doses twice a day) depending on the type and severity of infection. The total daily dose should not exceed 4 grams.

claims.text: Ceftriaxone penetrates the inflamed meninges of infants and pediatric patients; CSF concentrations were measured after 50 mg/kg and 75 mg/kg IV doses.
claims.byte_quote: Ceftriaxone penetrated the inflamed meninges of infants and pediatric patients; CSF concentrations after a 50 mg/kg IV dose and after a 75 mg/kg IV dose are also shown in Table 3 .

claims.text: Measured CSF concentration through inflamed meninges was 5.6 mcg/mL after the 50 mg/kg IV dose and 6.4 mcg/mL after the 75 mg/kg IV dose.
In neonates, intravenous ceftriaxone doses should be given over 60 minutes to reduce the risk of bilirubin encephalopathy (neonate-specific host/administration factor).
claims.byte_quote: Intravenous doses should be given over 60 minutes in neonates to reduce the risk of bilirubin encephalopathy.

claims.text: Ceftriaxone is bactericidal, acting by inhibition of bacterial cell wall synthesis, with activity in the presence of some beta-lactamases of both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria.
claims.byte_quote: Ceftriaxone is a bactericidal agent that acts by inhibition of bacterial cell wall synthesis. Ceftriaxone has activity in the presence of some beta-lactamases, both penicillinases and cephalosporinases, of Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria.
